name: Shakti 'Theta Band' random noise (T7 + T8, 10 min)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software); copies an accidental noise output of Persinger-lab (Laurentian University) DAC hardware in the early 1990s
summary: Murphy's 'Theta Band' signal: low-frequency noise with a 5.4 Hz spectral peak from one coil above each ear. Murphy reports that the accidental DAC noise it copies produced 'visions, vestibular sensations, and pleasant emotional effects'. The vendor calls it low-amplitude and less well tested; its file is not published, so the noise is rebuilt around that one number.
setting: Darkness and quiet (the vendor says effects during a session need darkness and silence); eyes closed, relaxed, without meditating or falling asleep; no meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor's Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break; try a session 2-3 times before changing it.
notes: The vendor titles the signal 'Low-Frequency, Low-Amplitude, Theta Band Noise'. Murphy's computer was not set up and the lab's ran too fast, and the output of both was 'possibly the same: No signal at all. The signal consisted of the noise from the DAC unit' (5jut4ranconsent.htm). The page gives a spectrum picture and one number, 'The peak frequency is 5.4hz', and the use: 'applying one signal to two coils, located above the ears, over both temporal lobes'; '10 minute sessions are usually sufficient', said of trying a signal out. This program plays 10 min of band-limited noise from 4 to 6.8 Hz, in 1-ms points, on two coils with the same signal (T7 and T8; the site names are this project's reading). The other six channels stay unused. The band limits around 5.4 Hz are this project's choice. The page also says 'the signals are amplitude modulated' and that the effect 'might also relate to the higher frequencies absent in the sine wave'; the narrow band here has neither. The noise is rebuilt from this description: the vendor's file is not published. Field strength: the vendor gives no number, only that the noise is low-amplitude, the output of a DAC that received no signal. The 1 uT default here is the strength of a full signal and has no source. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT there, the field is about 24 uT at the scalp. The support is Murphy's report. The vendor: 'Although his signal has been tried by a few people over both temporal lobes, no other presentations have been tried ... If you are not comfortable using less-well tested signals, do not use this one.' Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop at once if distressed.
source: Murphy, Shakti demo: Random Theta Band output (5jut4ran; 5.4 Hz FFT peak, also the LTP signal's peak) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/5jut4ranconsent.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Safety - how often https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/how_often_is_safe.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: How long should sessions be https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/safe_durations.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 (8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal, sham-controlled) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
